description: Measure a Rust project's test coverage — a single crate or a Cargo workspace, e.g. a command-line tool whose logic lives in `src/lib.rs` behind a thin `src/main.rs` — with cargo-llvm-cov (source-based LLVM coverage; `cargo llvm-cov nextest` when cargo-nextest is installed, plain `cargo llvm-cov` otherwise), always `--locked`, running the tests once with `--no-report` and then writing an lcov file (`target/coverage/lcov.info`, per-line hits) and a JSON summary (`target/coverage/summary.json`, per-file line/region/function figures), read with a small stdlib Python parser. Reports the exact line % (the gate figure) and region % for the total and per target file, with uncovered line ranges for every file under the bar; branch coverage is reported as unavailable on a stable toolchain (`--branch` needs nightly). Binaries spawned by end-to-end tests (assert_cmd's `Command::cargo_bin`) are instrumented too, so `src/main.rs` is measured fairly. Excludes `xtask/` (and any other tooling member) from the report with `--ignore-filename-regex`; `tests/` files are never reported; doctests don't count on stable (`--doctests` is nightly-only). Only container-free tests count — `#[ignore]` tests are never run here — and the report is still produced from a run with failing tests (labeled as such). Never uses `--fail-under-*`: it judges the bar itself. Invoke as `/iru-rust-coverage [targets]` — `[targets]` is a comma-separated list of source files (`src/commands/greet.rs`), directories (`src/commands/`), or module paths (`crate::output`, `commands::greet`, `<member_crate>::config`) — or `/iru-rust-coverage` with no argument for the whole workspace; optional `key: value` lines: `bar: <N>` (default 80), `package: <name>`, `features: all|<comma list>`, `filter: <test filter>` (a test-name substring, or `expr:<nextest filterset>`). Reports "coverage not wired" (cargo-llvm-cov or `llvm-tools-preview` missing) instead of a false 0%. Use whenever the user (or `iru-rust-code-one-task-group` via `iru-gate-runner`) wants to check, or verify a bar for, a Rust file, module, or the whole workspace, instead of eyeballing `cargo llvm-cov` tables.
